what: Pre-registered construction grid (width x weighting x neutrality x cost) rerun on the corrected ruler (surv panel: PIT mask + survivorship-complete), h=20, inverse-vol rows at 15bp. The 'capped' (75% long / 25% short) variant was added and pre-registered AFTER seeing that 50/50 neutral reversed its old verdict, as the only neutral structure deployable under the no-debt short cap (25% of equity). One iteration; disclosed.

verdicts.neutral_50_50: REVERSED vs the pre-correction grid: no longer hurts; cuts dev max drawdown ~40% with Sharpe mixed across widths (2 of 3 widths better on holdout, 1 of 3 on dev). Fails the pre-registered 'robust across widths' bar for adoption; and is not deployable under the 25% short cap anyway. Recorded as the lowest-drawdown structure.
verdicts.capped_75_25: REJECTED on attribution: its Sharpe advantage is beta harvest (market +8.7%/yr, beta 0.46) while the selection component drops from +3.0% to +1.2%/yr (IR 0.30 -> 0.13). Capping the short side removes half the stock-picking alpha and replaces it with market drift.
verdicts.width_30_50: Within noise: dev 0.22 -> 0.31 at n=30 with holdout 0.85 -> 0.78. Not adopted on its own; kept as the natural width once the universe grows (full-breadth test pending). n=30 also needs the $1M paper reset.
verdicts.production: NO CHANGE. Raw top-10 inverse-vol stays. On the corrected ruler it is already near-neutral (beta 0.02) and carries the full selection component.

lesson: Sharpe alone cannot adjudicate a construction change on a long-biased-capable book; the risk-model attribution must accompany every grid cell, or the same beta-for-alpha mistake that inflated the retracted 0.8 headline returns through the construction door.
